chunks: It is recommended for the Muslim to have intercourse with his wife on the first night of the month of Ramadan, due to the saying of Allah, the Blessed and Exalted: 'Permitted to you, on the night of the fasts, is the approach to your wives.'

And 'approach' means sexual intercourse. Do not wear rings other than silver, for the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'A hand upon which there is an iron ring is not clean.'
And whoever engraves the Name of Allah, the Exalted, on his ring, he should move it to the hand he uses for cleansing himself after urination.

When one of you looks in the mirror, he should say: 'Praise be to Allah who created me and perfected my creation, and fashioned me and perfected my form, and adorned me with what He did not adorn others with, and honored me with Islam.'
And let one of you adorn himself for his Muslim brother when he visits him, as he would adorn himself for a stranger whom he loves to see in the best state.
Fasting three days of every month: Wednesday between two Thursdays. And fasting in the month of Sha'ban removes the whispers of the chest and the disturbances of the heart.
Cleansing oneself with cold water cuts off hemorrhoids.
And washing clothes removes anxiety and sadness, and it is a purification for prayer.
Do not pluck out grey hair, for it is the light of the Muslim. And whoever acquires a grey hair while in Islam, it will be a light for him on the Day of Resurrection.

The Muslim should not sleep while in a state of major impurity (junub), nor should he sleep except in a state of purity. If he does not find water, he should perform dry ablution (tayammum) with earth, for the spirit of the believer is raised to Allah, the Blessed and Exalted, who accepts it and blesses it. If his time of death has arrived, He places it in the treasures of His mercy. If his time has not arrived, He sends it back with His trusted angels, who return it to his body.
The believer should not spit in the direction of the Qibla. If he does so unintentionally, he should seek forgiveness from Allah, the Exalted.
The man should not blow at the place of his prostration, nor at his food, nor at his drink, nor at his charm.

The man should not sleep on the thoroughfare. And let him not urinate from a height into the air, nor in hot water. If he does so and something happens to him, let him blame only himself, for water has its inhabitants and air has its inhabitants.
The man should not sleep on his face. And whoever you see sleeping on his face, wake him up and do not let him continue.

Let not one of you stand in prayer lazily or drowsily, nor think about himself, for he is in the presence of his Lord, the Exalted. And the servant receives from his prayer only that which he offers with his heart.
Eat what falls from the tablecloth, for it is a cure for every disease by the permission of Allah, the Exalted, for whoever wishes to seek cure through it.
When one of you eats food, let him lick the fingers with which he ate. Allah, the Exalted, says: 'May Allah bless you.'
Wear cotton clothing, for it is the clothing of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) and it is our clothing. We did not wear hair or wool except due to a necessity.
And He said: 'Indeed, Allah, the Exalted, is Beautiful and loves beauty, and He loves to see the effect of His blessing upon His servant.'

Maintain ties with your relatives, even with a greeting. Allah, the Blessed and Exalted, says: 'And fear Allah through whom you ask one another, and the wombs. Indeed, Allah is ever, over you, a Observer.'
Do not waste your day with 'so-and-so' and 'so-and-so' and 'we did such and such', for there are angels with you who record your deeds.
Remember Allah in every place, for He is with you.

Send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad, for Allah, the Exalted, accepts your supplications when you remember Muhammad, and your supplications for him, and your protection of him, peace be upon him and his family.

Let the hot food cool down until it is cool, for the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) was brought food and he said: 'Let it cool until it is cool and can be eaten. Would Allah, the Exalted, feed us fire? And the blessing is in the cool.'
When one of you urinates, let him not aim his urine into the air, nor face the wind.
Teach your children what benefits them from Allah. Let the Murji'ah not overpower them with their opinion.
Restrain your tongues and greet with peace, and you will gain.
Return the trust to whoever entrusted you with it, even to the killers of the children of the Prophets, peace be upon them.

Increase the remembrance of Allah, the Exalted, when you enter the markets while people are busy, for it is an expiation for sins and an increase in good deeds. And do not be recorded among the heedless.
It is not for the servant to travel when the month of Ramadan arrives, due to the saying of Allah, the Exalted: 'Whoever among you sights the month, let him fast it.'
there is no concealment of faith (taqiyyah) regarding drinking intoxicants and wiping over the foot-coverings.

key_terms.الرَّفَثُ: Sexual intercourse or approach to wives

ai.seo_question: What are the recommended ethical and ritual practices for Muslims according to Imam Ali in al-Khisal?
ai.summary: This compilation from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Al-Khisal* preserves a dense transmission of Imam Ali’s (peace be upon him) practical wisdom, blending ritual purity (*taharah*) with social ethics (*adab*) in a format characteristic of early Shia oral teaching traditions. The inclusion of specific legal nuances, such as the permissibility of silver rings and the prohibition of spitting toward the Qibla, highlights the text's role in codifying daily devotional practices for the lay community. These guidelines reflect the Shia emphasis on integrating spiritual mindfulness into mundane acts, from marital intimacy to dining etiquette.
